title: U.S. House · Ohio's 4th District
area: North-central Ohio, including Lima and Mansfield

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 4th District R+21, a safely Republican-leaning seat.

candidates.name: Jim Jordan
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Jordan is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th District, first elected in 2006, and chairs the House Judiciary Committee.

background.text: Born in Troy, Ohio; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin (1986), a master's degree from Ohio State University (1991), and a law degree from Capital University (2001).

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on the Judiciary and serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Kolasinski is a business owner running as the Democratic nominee, with a platform centered on government accountability, economic opportunity for workers, and healthcare cost reform.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from Owens Community College and a bachelor's degree from Siena Heights University; works as a business owner.

priorities.text: Campaign website calls for government accountability and transparency, including a 'Registered Voter Lobby' and a district think tank, and says full-time work 'deserves economic stability.'
Campaign website calls for healthcare reform, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices and increasing price transparency.
Campaign website calls for getting 'big money out of politics,' including repealing Citizens United, banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and supporting term limits.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices and exploring public and private options to reduce healthcare costs.
positions.quote: Allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices. Increase price transparency so patients know costs before care.

summary.text: Tackett is the Assistant Mayor of Springfield, Ohio and a development manager at Glen Helen Nature Preserve, running as an independent on a platform of local empowerment and government accountability.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in organizational leadership and political science from Wittenberg University (2022) and a master's degree in public policy and leadership from Ohio State University's John Glenn College of Public Affairs (2024).
Serves as Assistant Mayor of Springfield, Ohio and as Development Manager for Glen Helen Nature Preserve; is also a small-business owner.

priorities.text: Says she is an independent who believes 'solving problems is more important than partisan fighting' and will work with anyone with a good idea.
priorities.quote: I'm an Independent who believes solving problems is more important than partisan fighting.

priorities.text: Says decisions should empower local governments and institutions, and pledges to 'bring resources back home, support first responders, strengthen infrastructure.'
Calls for fiscal responsibility and government transparency, and for supporting agriculture and small businesses.
